name: Jubail
title: UTM Thickness Gauging in Jubail: Chemical Tankers & Hulls
description: Ultrasonic thickness gauging in Jubail for chemical tankers, gas carriers and bulk ships: ESP tank gauging, CAP scopes and pre-docking hull structure work.
h1: Thickness Gauging for Chemical Tankers, Gas Carriers and Bulk Ships in Jubail
intro: Jubail's ports exist to ship what Jubail Industrial City makes. Chemical and product tankers, gas carriers and bulk carriers lift petrochemicals, fuels, fertilisers and metals from the plants around King Fahd Industrial Port and Ras Al-Khair. Their owners face extensive cargo-area gauging under the enhanced survey rules, and their charterers expect tank structure to be documented. We mobilise a team from India to Jubail and gauge cargo and ballast tanks, hull structure and deck piping between parcels, at anchorage or ahead of a docking.

highlights.p: Coated and stainless cargo tanks, the ballast tanks and double bottoms around them, and the deck cargo and heating lines all age differently. We plan readings to the enhanced survey rules for chemical tankers under IACS UR Z10.3 and to the charterer's concerns.

highlights.h: Work between parcels and at anchorage
highlights.p: Chemical tankers often load several grades at several Jubail berths. Tanks cleaned and gas-freed between parcels, and waits at the anchorage for the next jetty, are the windows where cargo-area gauging fits without delaying the ship.

Bulk carriers loading at Ras Al-Khair and King Fahd Industrial Port carry cargoes whose residues attack hold steel in humid heat. We gauge frames, hopper plating and tank tops, and add crack detection where coatings have broken down.

port.h: Jubail Industrial City and Its Ports
p: Jubail was built as a planned industrial city, administered by the Royal Commission for Jubail and Yanbu, and its plants include SABIC affiliates, the Sadara chemical complex and the SATORP refinery. Two Mawani ports serve it. King Fahd Industrial Port handles the liquid and dry bulk of the industrial city: petrochemicals, refined products, liquefied gases, fertilisers and metals going out, feedstock and materials coming in. Jubail Commercial Port takes containers, general cargo, steel and project cargo. North along the coast, Ras Al-Khair Port serves the Ma'aden phosphate and aluminium complex, adding fertiliser and mineral bulk carriers to the mix.

The liquid side shapes the fleet. Chemical tankers here frequently load part cargoes at more than one Jubail berth, then top up at other Eastern Province or UAE ports, so a ship can spend days moving between jetties and the anchorage. Tank cleaning and gas-freeing between grades, ballast legs and berth waits create the windows in which cargo-area gauging is possible. Gas carriers load ammonia and other liquefied petrochemical gases for export, and bulk carriers can wait at anchorage for loading slots at the fertiliser berths, which gives time to open and inspect holds before the cargo goes in.

The inspection demand that results is technical rather than routine. Chemical tankers have their own IACS enhanced survey rule, UR Z10.3, and by the third renewal survey the cargo-area gauging is extensive. Many carry cargoes heated, which warms adjacent ballast tanks and double bottoms already sitting in hot, saline Gulf water, and coating failure there advances quickly. Stainless cargo tanks rarely waste, but the carbon-steel structure around them does, and deck lines, heating coils and manifold pipework suffer from both cargo and climate. Bulk carriers that have carried fertilisers or sulphur suffer from acidic residues in humid holds, and gauging finds thinning on frames, brackets and hopper plates.

facilities.h: Where Gauging Is Done in Jubail and Ras Al-Khair
p: Almost all gauging in Jubail is done afloat. At the liquid berths of King Fahd Industrial Port, terminal safety rules govern who boards and what work is allowed, so tank entry and gauging during a loading call need the terminal's agreement as well as the master's, and the tank must be certified gas-free. The anchorage gives more freedom: a ship waiting for its next jetty can open, ventilate and gauge cargo and ballast tanks with no other cargo operation nearby. At Jubail Commercial Port, general cargo and container ships can be gauged during cargo work on deck, in holds and in accessible tanks.

Jubail has no long-established drydock of its own. International Maritime Industries (IMI) is building up a large shipbuilding and repair yard at Ras Al-Khair, north of the city, and the Zamil yard in Dammam and ASRY in Bahrain are within reach for docking. For any of them, gauging the cargo area in Jubail before the ship leaves gives the repair specification real figures, and leaves the in-dock days for the bottom, the sea chests and the areas that can only be reached in dock.
list: King Fahd Industrial Port liquid berths — cargo tank, deck line and heating coil gauging on chemical tankers between parcels, with terminal and master agreement
Jubail anchorage — full cargo and ballast tank gauging on chemical and product tankers waiting for their next jetty, reached by launch
Jubail Commercial Port — hold, hatch cover and deck gauging on general cargo, multipurpose and container ships during cargo operations
Ras Al-Khair Port — hold frame, hopper plate and tank top gauging on bulk carriers loading fertiliser and minerals
IMI yard, Ras Al-Khair — pre-docking and in-dock gauging for ships booked into the yard International Maritime Industries is building up there
Gas carrier loading berths — hull, ballast tank and deck piping gauging on gas carriers, moved to the anchorage when the loading stay is too short

context.h: Chemical Tanker Rules, Vetting and Regulation in Jubail
p: Ships in Jubail come under the Riyadh MoU for port state control, and inspectors at an industrial port pay close attention to cargo systems and deck structure. The heavier structural requirements come from the enhanced survey programme. SOLAS chapter XI-1 regulation 2 and the 2011 ESP Code make enhanced surveys mandatory for oil tankers and bulk carriers; for chemical tankers the equivalent requirements come through class under IACS UR Z10.3. In each case, areas of substantial corrosion found at one survey are measured again at the surveys that follow, which is where planned gauging between surveys saves the owner time in port.

Commercial pressure is as strong as regulation. Chemical tankers face inspection by the oil majors and by the Chemical Distribution Institute, and charterers lifting from Jubail's plants look at tank coatings and structure when choosing tonnage; older product and chemical tankers are often asked for CAP. For these owners, thickness measurement in Saudi Arabia is as much a vetting matter as a class one. The Gulf is outside any emission control area, so the 0.50% global sulphur cap applies, and scrubbers are more common on the larger tankers and bulk carriers calling here than on small chemical parcel tankers. Saudi Arabia is also building up maritime industry at home, and the Ras Al-Khair yard is part of that effort.

jobs.h: Typical thickness gauging jobs in Jubail
jobs.p: Ship inspection in Jubail centres on the cargo area. Most jobs are planned around a chemical tanker's parcel schedule or a bulk carrier's wait for a loading slot, and they feed an approaching survey, a charterer's request or a docking specification. Because the ships are rarely idle for long, the scope is agreed tank by tank with the chief officer, and the team works through whichever spaces are gas-free and ventilated on the day while the rest of the plan waits for the next window.
list: A stainless-steel chemical tanker at the Jubail anchorage: double-bottom and wing ballast tanks gauged between parcels to give the owner corrosion trends before its third renewal survey
A coated-tank product and chemical tanker: CAP-scope gauging of cargo tank deckheads, bulkheads and deck longitudinals, requested by a charterer before fixing the ship
A bulk carrier waiting to load fertiliser at Ras Al-Khair: hold frame, bracket and hopper plate gauging, with magnetic particle testing at frame end connections
A gas carrier between loadings: ballast tanks, double-bottom structure under the cargo tank supports and deck piping gauged at anchorage
A chemical tanker bound for docking: deck cargo lines and heating coils gauged in Jubail so that pipe renewal can be ordered before the ship reaches the yard

logistics: Jubail is reached through King Fahd International Airport near Dammam, with the team continuing north by road. King Fahd Industrial Port sits inside a controlled industrial city, so gate passes are tighter than at a commercial port: the ship's agent applies for them with each technician's passport and visa details, and terminal safety induction may be required before boarding. Anchorage work needs a launch from the port, again through the agent. Indian technicians travel on Saudi business visit visas, so we begin the application when the ship's parcel schedule settles and adjust travel as berth times move.

faqs.q: Can you gauge cargo tanks on a chemical tanker between parcels in Jubail?
faqs.a: Yes, where the tank has been cleaned, ventilated and certified gas-free and the terminal allows entry. In practice the anchorage is the easier place: once the ship has finished at one jetty and is waiting for the next, the chief officer can release tanks in turn. We work through them in the order they become available and record which spaces remain for the next opportunity.

faqs.q: Do stainless steel cargo tanks need thickness measurement?
faqs.a: Stainless cargo tanks seldom lose thickness to general corrosion, and the attending surveyor decides whether readings are needed there. The carbon-steel structure around them, meaning ballast tanks, double bottoms, cofferdams and deck, corrodes like any other ship's steel in Gulf service. Gauging on a stainless chemical tanker therefore concentrates on those spaces and on any pitting found during visual inspection of the cargo tanks.

faqs.q: Our bulk carrier is loading at Ras Al-Khair. Can you gauge the holds first?
faqs.a: Holds can be gauged while the ship waits for its loading slot, provided they are clean and dry and access is safe. Fertiliser and similar residues, combined with Gulf humidity, attack frames, brackets and lower hopper plating, so we focus there and use magnetic particle testing at frame end connections where coatings have failed. Once loading starts, hold gauging is no longer practical.

faqs.q: Where do Jubail ships go to drydock, and can you gauge there too?
faqs.a: Ships from Jubail dock at a range of yards: ASRY in Bahrain, the Zamil yard in Dammam for smaller vessels, yards in the UAE and further afield, with the IMI yard at Ras Al-Khair building up its own role. We can gauge in Jubail before departure, at the docking yard, or both, sending a team from India to whichever location suits the repair schedule.
